headline: New York Delivers $189M in Summer Food Aid to 1.6M Children
meta_description: New York provided $189 million in summer food assistance to nearly 1.6 million children, filling a critical gap when free school lunches end each June.
summary_short: New York delivered $189 million in summer food assistance to nearly 1.6 million children this summer, addressing hunger when school meals disappear.
body:
New York delivered $189 million in summer food assistance to nearly 1.6 million children this summer, closing a crucial gap that emerges every June when free school lunches end.

The program recognizes a persistent challenge facing low-income families: the summer months create a hunger crisis when the safety net of school meals vanishes. Without intervention, children who depend on these meals during the academic year face food insecurity during the longest school break. By channeling nearly $189 million directly to support summer nutrition, New York addressed this seasonal vulnerability head-on.

The scale of the initiative—reaching 1.6 million children across the state—demonstrates a commitment to ensuring that economic hardship doesn't translate into childhood hunger during the vulnerable summer period. Programs like this acknowledge that food security isn't a year-round given for many families, and that thoughtful policy can bridge the gap.
quick_facts: $189 million delivered in summer food assistance
Addresses hunger gap when school lunches end in June
